summary: Taliban troops claim they are closing in on and pursuing Hamid Karzai in the mountains of Oruzgan province after attacking his hideout, though Karzai says he is safe and managed to fight them off.
Hamid Karzai is named leader of Afghanistan's transitional government.
Hamid Karzai is named head of a six-month caretaker government for Afghanistan.

Rival groups reportedly reach agreement on the future of Kandahar and rebel Northern Alliance warlord Gen Abdul Rashid Dostam endorses Kabul's power-sharing government, boosting new Afghan leader Hamid Karzai.
Hamid Karzai, head of Afghanistan's interim government, arrived in Kabul, marking what may be the capital's first peaceful transfer of power in decades.
An international pledging conference in Tokyo promises swift assistance to Hamid Karzai's interim Afghan government, with pledges potentially exceeding the $1.7bn needed this year.
Countries at a Tokyo conference pledge $4.5bn in aid to Afghanistan, conditional on Hamid Karzai's interim government making progress toward democracy.
Interim leader Hamid Karzai announced a 21-member commission charged with summoning a loya jirga to decide Afghanistan's transitional government.
Hamid Karzai stepped up from chairman of the transitional administration to interim president after King Zahir Shah stood aside.
Afghan security officials arrest hundreds in connection with an alleged plot to bomb Kabul and overthrow interim prime minister Hamid Karzai's government.
Afghan security forces in Kabul arrested hundreds of people from the hardline Hezb-i-Islami group after uncovering an apparent plot to overthrow interim government head Hamid Karzai.
Hamid Karzai will fly to Rome to collect former king Zahir Shah and return with him to Kabul, possibly by tomorrow.
Hamid Karzai, leader of Afghanistan's interim government, flanked former king Zahir Shah as he returned to Kabul from 29 years of exile.
Hamid Karzai appeared to have won the support of enough key allies to stay on as head of the Afghan government for the next two years.

Hamid Karzai apparently succeeded in winning a second term as Afghanistan's leader after the loya jirga opened, with former king Zahir Shah urging delegates to support him and rival Burhanuddin Rabbani bowing out of the race.
Hamid Karzai was overwhelmingly elected head of state by Afghanistan's loya jirga, winning 1,295 votes and taking charge of an interim government until elections in 2004.
Hamid Karzai, newly elected Afghan leader, was scheduled to address the loya jirga as mass walkouts occurred amid disputes over the legislature.
Hamid Karzai, newly elected president of Afghanistan, delays naming his cabinet for one more day, telling the loya jirga he needs additional time to form a government acceptable to everyone.
Hamid Karzai named an executive cabinet for an 18-month transitional administration, dividing key ministries between ethnic Tajiks and Pashtuns.
Afghan Vice President Haji Abdul Qadir, a key Pashtun ally of President Hamid Karzai, is assassinated, leaving Karzai without a key ally in the center and facing a potential power vacuum in the east.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai survived an assassination attempt when a gunman fired four rounds into his car as he left the Kandahar governor's mansion; the attacker was shot dead by US special forces.
The US State Department confirmed that Hamid Karzai's US military bodyguards were replaced by a private security detail managed by the Diplomatic Security Service and involving DynCorp personnel.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai outlined plans at an international conference in Bonn to boost the fledgling national army, proposing a 70,000-strong force and the disarmament of former fighters.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai held nearly two hours of talks with Tony Blair at Downing Street and lunched with Blair, Jack Straw, and other cabinet ministers during his three-day official visit to Britain.
Hamid Karzai appeals for up to $15bn in reconstruction assistance on top of $5bn previously pledged, with Afghanistan's finance minister saying funds received so far have been inadequate.
Suspected Taliban fighters attacked a police station in Paktika province, Afghanistan, in the latest attempt to destabilize Hamid Karzai's pro-US government.
Former warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum announced he will challenge US-supported Hamid Karzai in Afghanistan's October presidential election.

Interim president Hamid Karzai announced he would stand as a candidate in Afghanistan's first direct presidential election, dropping defence minister Mohammed Fahim from his ticket and naming Ahmad Zia Massood and Karim Khalili as vice-presidential running mates.

Pakistan's President Pervez Musharraf offered unqualified help to interim Afghan leader Hamid Karzai against Taliban insurgents threatening Afghanistan's presidential elections, vowing that anyone trying to disrupt the election process would not be allowed from Pakistan.
Interim Afghan president Hamid Karzai moved to dismiss Ismail Khan as governor of Herat, prompting riots in which at least seven people died.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai evaded an apparent assassination attempt when a rocket attack missed his helicopter as he was landing in Gardez.
Hamid Karzai's running mate, Ahmed Zia Massoud, narrowly escaped an assassination attempt by the Taliban when a roadside bomb exploded as his convoy passed in Faizabad.
A roadside bomb attacked a convoy carrying Hamid Karzai's vice-presidential running mate, Ahmed Zia Massood, three days before the Afghan presidential election; Massood was unharmed but one man died.

An American-conducted exit poll predicts Hamid Karzai will win Afghanistan's presidential election by enough votes to avoid a run-off, after opposition challenger Yunus Qanooni withdrew his boycott threat.

Hamid Karzai's share of the vote in Afghanistan's presidential election passed the 50% mark with 94% of ballots counted, putting him on course to avoid a run-off, though official confirmation was frozen pending an investigation into alleged polling irregularities.

Hamid Karzai won over 55% of votes in the Afghan election, securing enough to become the country's first popularly elected president, though official confirmation was pending an investigation into alleged polling irregularities.
Hamid Karzai was declared the winner of Afghanistan's landmark presidential election, securing over 55% of the vote and a five-year term.
Hamid Karzai was sworn in as Afghanistan's first popularly elected president, pledging to crack down on the opium trade, disarm militias, and raise living standards.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai used a meeting with visiting US Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld to lobby for a long-term security partnership with the US, though neither committed to a permanent US military presence.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai departs for the US, promising to confront George Bush over American abuse of Afghan prisoners.
Hamid Karzai stood with George Bush in Kabul as Bush praised Afghanistan's progress, while Karzai's power was described as barely extending beyond the capital.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai and other ministers complain about the lack of coordination and intelligence-sharing between US and NATO forces and their Afghan counterparts after a US air strike mistakenly killed eight Afghan policemen.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai announced the death of former King Mohammad Zahir Shah, declared three days of national mourning, and ordered flags flown at half-mast.

At a Camp David press conference with Afghan President Hamid Karzai, President George W. Bush said the US would kill Osama bin Laden and other al-Qaida leaders in Pakistan if it had actionable intelligence, exposing tensions over Pakistan's tribal areas; Karzai also described Iran as a "helper" to Afghanistan, differing from the US view.
Hamid Karzai withdrew his support for Lord Ashdown's appointment as UN envoy to Afghanistan, leading Ashdown to withdraw his application.
President Hamid Karzai survived a Taliban assassination attempt during a military parade in central Kabul.
Eight Afghan security officials, including the top civilian counterterrorism official and Kabul's police chief, were suspended after an assassination attempt on President Hamid Karzai.
Hamid Karzai threatened to send Afghan troops across the border into Pakistan to hunt down the Taliban's leadership.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai threatened to send troops across the border into Pakistan to hunt Taliban leadership.

A spokesman for Afghan President Hamid Karzai says the government has "sufficient evidence" indicating Pakistan's intelligence agency was behind the Indian embassy bombing in Kabul that killed 41 people.
Afghanistan's election commission announces the presidential election will be delayed until 20 August, effectively extending President Hamid Karzai's term beyond the five years he was elected to.
Hamid Karzai offers to provide security for Taliban leader Mullah Omar if he agrees to enter peace talks, saying the US and other nations could remove him as Afghanistan's president if they disagree.
Hamid Karzai admitted to a senior UN official that Brahamdagh Bugti was in Kabul, according to US embassy cables.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai told U.S. Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Flournoy that his government welcomed the opportunity to join the U.S. strategic policy review and suggested priorities including targeting terrorist leaders and sanctuaries in Pakistan, strengthening Afghan communities, and holding talks with Taliban groups willing to respect the Afghan constitution.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai calls for a snap presidential election to be held before 21 April, despite the independent election commission's warning that millions of voters would be disenfranchised.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai agreed to postpone the country's presidential elections from April to 20 August after the independent election commission ruled to delay them due to security and logistical problems.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai warned the international community not to interfere in Afghanistan's government as it prepares for presidential elections.

The US and European allies are preparing to create a new chief executive or prime ministerial role in the Kabul government aimed at bypassing Afghan President Hamid Karzai, as part of a White House review of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Afghan politicians, including former finance minister Ashraf Ghani and former vice-president Hedayat Amin Arsala, plan to stand against President Hamid Karzai in the August presidential election amid widespread criticism of his leadership, corruption, and governance.
Influential Afghan governor Gul Agha Sherzai said he will not run for president, leaving incumbent Hamid Karzai in an increasingly strong position to win re-election.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai selects former warlord Mohammad Qasim Fahim as a vice-presidential running mate for the 20 August presidential election, defying international pressure.
Hamid Karzai met with Barack Obama and Asif Ali Zardari at the White House, where Obama urged the Afghan and Pakistani leaders to take a tougher stance against the Taliban.
Hamid Karzai pulled out of Afghanistan's first televised presidential debate hours before it was due to be broadcast, claiming his policies were not ready.
Afghan presidential candidates Abdullah Abdullah and Ashraf Ghani campaign against incumbent Hamid Karzai ahead of the 20 August election, criticizing his record on development and security.

Hamid Karzai held his first campaign rally outside Kabul in the village of Kayan, relying on the endorsement of Ismaili spiritual leader Syed Mansoor Nadiri to turn out voters ahead of the August 20 presidential election.
Hamid Karzai participated in a televised election debate with leading competitors, though second-place candidate Abdullah Abdullah did not attend.

Hamid Karzai faces a crisis of legitimacy and a legal challenge to his re-election if proclaimed the outright winner of Afghanistan's presidential ballot, as his chief rival Abdullah Abdullah accused him of "stealing" the election.
Both Hamid Karzai and Abdullah Abdullah claimed victory in Afghanistan's presidential election, despite US calls for candidates to refrain from claiming victory before official results.
First results from Afghanistan's presidential election give incumbent Hamid Karzai a narrow lead over Abdullah Abdullah with 41% to 39% of ballots processed so far.
Hamid Karzai extended his lead in Afghanistan's presidential election as fraud allegations mounted and the British ambassador warned vote rigging could determine the outcome.

Hamid Karzai passed the 50% threshold in Afghanistan's presidential election with 54.1% of the vote based on results from 91.6% of polling stations counted, though a partial recount was ordered after observers found clear and convincing evidence of fraud.

Hamid Karzai's chances of being elected president through genuine elections were good, but his "victory-through-fraud" shows he hasn't learned basic international democratic norms since he was first voted in in 2004.
Ballots from about a tenth of Afghanistan's polling stations are to be recounted after evidence surfaced of widespread fraud, possibly forcing President Hamid Karzai to face another round of voting.
Fears mount in Kabul that Hamid Karzai will refuse to accept the results of an official inquiry into massive electoral fraud, which is expected to trigger a second round of voting.

The UN-backed Electoral Complaints Commission declared hundreds of thousands of votes for Afghan President Hamid Karzai invalid, stripping him of outright victory and triggering a second-round runoff against Abdullah Abdullah.
A UN-backed election watchdog invalidated hundreds of thousands of votes for Hamid Karzai in Afghanistan's disputed August election, reducing his total to 48.3% and setting the stage for a runoff.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai agreed to a second-round runoff in Afghanistan's election after accepting a UN-backed fraud investigation that stripped him of nearly 1 million votes and his first-round majority.
Ahmed Wali Karzai, the younger brother of Afghan president Hamid Karzai, was reported to have been on the CIA's payroll for almost eight years, allegations he denied.
Hamid Karzai was declared re-elected as president of Afghanistan, ending an election widely regarded as fraudulent.

Abdullah Abdullah withdrew from Afghanistan's presidential runoff election, throwing the race into disarray and pushing Western backers to seek a rapid coronation of Hamid Karzai as president without a second round of voting.
Afghan officials declared Hamid Karzai the winner of the country's disputed presidential election after cancelling a planned runoff.
Hamid Karzai vows to tackle corruption and reach out to political opponents in his first speech since being re-appointed as president of Afghanistan.
Hamid Karzai was re-elected for another five years, a result that was not reported by state-run RTA television, which aired a Tom and Jerry cartoon instead.
Hamid Karzai was sworn in for a second term as Afghanistan's president at a tightly guarded ceremony in Kabul.

Afghanistan's chief prosecutor announces an unprecedented attempt to prosecute two sitting cabinet members of Hamid Karzai's government for corruption, which cannot proceed until Karzai strips them of ministerial immunity.
The US seeks to appoint an international "high representative" in Kabul to bypass Hamid Karzai's government, causing a split with NATO allies.

The UN's top diplomat in Afghanistan, Kai Eide, condemned proposals to install a powerful high representative in Kabul to deal with President Hamid Karzai, saying the idea would bypass and undermine the Afghan government.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai opened a three-day anti-corruption conference in Kabul, saying he was aware of the scale of the problem but warning that an all-out crackdown urged by Western allies could lead to abuses.
A suicide car bomber struck a Kabul hotel as Afghan President Hamid Karzai was due to attend an anti-corruption conference elsewhere in the city; Karzai later condemned the attack.
Hamid Karzai is under intense western pressure to take more serious action against corruption at the start of a critical conference in London about Afghanistan's future.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai unveiled a peace plan at a London conference to reconcile with Taliban fighters who are not part of al-Qaida and accept the Afghan constitution.
Pakistan arrests senior Afghan Taliban leaders, including deputy commander Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, disrupting secret UN-backed talks between the Karzai government and the Taliban.
Hamid Karzai takes personal control of Afghanistan's electoral process by presidential decree, neutering the Electoral Complaints Commission.

Britain urges Afghan President Hamid Karzai's government to put more effort into pursuing peace talks, with Foreign Secretary David Miliband warning that Karzai's proposed loya jirga could be little more than a PR stunt.
Afghanistan's parliament voted overwhelmingly to overturn President Hamid Karzai's February decree that had given him the right to appoint all five members of the Electoral Complaints Commission.

Former UN deputy head Peter Galbraith suggested on US television that Hamid Karzai has a substance abuse problem and questioned his mental stability, prompting a presidential spokesman to reject the claims.

The Obama administration rolls out the red carpet for Afghan President Hamid Karzai during a four-day visit to Washington, granting him unprecedented access to top US officials despite simmering tensions.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai and US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton met to smooth over recent public disagreements between Kabul and Washington over Taliban strategy and corruption in Afghanistan.
G8 leaders demand that Afghan President Hamid Karzai present detailed plans to take over security responsibility and tackle corruption within five years.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai is reported to be shocked by the size of the leak of classified US military documents, though his spokesman says the substance is mostly not new and the government will not seek to exploit it.

Hamid Karzai calls on NATO to destroy insurgent sanctuaries in Pakistan, saying the war on terrorism is not based in Afghanistan but in sanctuaries, funding centres and training places outside Afghanistan.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai criticised American plans to start withdrawing troops next summer, saying the named date has given the Taliban insurgency a morale boost.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai wept as he appealed to compatriots to "come to their senses" on the day his government launched a 68-member "high peace council" to oversee negotiations to end the war with the Taliban.

Abdul Qayum Karzai, brother of President Hamid Karzai, described to the U.S. Ambassador the potential Saudi reconciliation process with the Taliban, which he had developed with Abdullah Anas and which had secured Taliban engagement through Mullah Abdul Salam Zaif.

Reports of recent contacts between senior Taliban and the Kabul government under President Hamid Karzai are described by diplomats and observers as mostly hype, involving little more than exchanges of cash and prisoners rather than a genuine peace settlement.
WikiLeaks cables released by the US embassy portray Afghan President Hamid Karzai as corrupt, erratic, and prone to paranoid conspiracy theories, according to diplomats and foreign statesmen.

US diplomats in Kabul fear WikiLeaks cables portraying Hamid Karzai and his government in a deeply unflattering light will further weaken US-Afghan relations, with the US embassy engaged in damage limitation.

WikiLeaks cables reveal that Afghan President Hamid Karzai was described by diplomats as erratic, emotional, and prone to paranoid conspiracy theories, and was accused by his own ministers of complicity in criminal activity.
Afghanistan's finance minister warns that the release of leaked US diplomatic cables portraying President Hamid Karzai and his government unfavorably will damage Afghanistan's relations with the US.
David Cameron meets Afghan President Hamid Karzai in Kabul for talks on progress in Afghanistan and transition to Afghan-led security, acknowledging leaked cables raised embarrassing questions.

Hamid Karzai promised that the Afghan people would decide the terms for US forces to remain in Afghanistan after the 2014 pullout, through a loya jirga once Washington and Kabul finish negotiating a long-term deal.
Hamid Karzai's second cousin, Haji Yar Mohammad Karzai, was accidentally killed by US special forces during a botched night raid in Karz, Kandahar province.
Thousands of Afghans attend a rally in Kabul opposing peace talks with the Taliban, criticizing President Hamid Karzai's efforts to reach out to the Taliban.
Ahmed Wali Karzai, the half-brother of Afghan President Hamid Karzai, was assassinated by one of his security guards inside his house in Kandahar.
Jan Muhammad Khan, a close ally and mentor of Hamid Karzai, is killed when two gunmen storm his walled compound in Kabul, a week after the assassination of Karzai's half-brother Ahmed Wali Karzai.
Taliban insurgents attack the base of Matiullah Khan, a powerful warlord and key ally of Hamid Karzai, in Tirin Kot, Uruzgan, killing at least 17 people; Khan is unharmed.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai issued a decree intended to resolve Afghanistan's disputed parliamentary election, but its ambiguity led both supporters of the special court and the Independent Electoral Commission to claim victory, leaving the 11-month standoff unresolved.
Burhanuddin Rabbani, President Hamid Karzai's main peace envoy, was killed by a suicide bomber in Kabul.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai said in an interview on Geo Television that Afghanistan would side with Pakistan if the US attacked Pakistan.
Hamid Karzai told a loya jirga that he will not sign a military pact with the US until night raids by foreign forces end.

A four-day loya jirga, dismissed by critics as a rubber stamp for Hamid Karzai's decisions, is due to start in Kabul to debate a long-term military and economic pact with the US, amid death threats, boycotts by more than 100 MPs, and Taliban threats to attack the gathering.
Hamid Karzai demands that the US hand over control of its main military prison in Afghanistan, the detention centre at Parwan, within a month.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai confronted Pakistani leadership in Islamabad, demanding Pakistan bring Taliban leaders to the negotiating table, with his aggressive tone causing the Pakistani prime minister to halt a full delegation meeting.

Hamid Karzai told NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen that the US-Afghan strategic partnership cannot be signed until foreign troops hand over all jails to Afghan control and stop night raids.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai said he would meet western demands to sign a much-delayed strategic partnership pact with the US by May, before the NATO summit in Chicago, though the agreement may not initially establish the size or location of US forces remaining in Afghanistan.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai said he is considering stepping down a year early, potentially moving the 2014 presidential election to 2013.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai blamed intelligence failures, especially by Nato, for an 18-hour Taliban siege of Kabul and simultaneous attacks across eastern Afghanistan, and called for an investigation.
A former Taliban minister turned government peace negotiator, Arsala Rahmani, was shot dead in Kabul, a blow to President Hamid Karzai's hopes of bringing the Taliban to the negotiating table.
Barack Obama is to use the NATO summit to press Afghan President Hamid Karzai to engage with greater urgency with the Taliban about a political settlement in Afghanistan.
Pakistan agreed to release Taliban prisoners as part of efforts by Hamid Karzai to start a peace process with the Taliban.
Barack Obama met with Afghan President Hamid Karzai to discuss arrangements for Afghanistan after the formal withdrawal of US and other coalition forces at the end of 2014.
Hamid Karzai says he will step down as president of Afghanistan next year and take a long holiday, as the constitution bars him from running in another election.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai stayed at Claridge's hotel in London with an entourage of 40 officials for talks with Pakistan's president Asif Ali Zardari, the same day he issued a decree back home to curtail government expenses.

President Hamid Karzai is determined to curb CIA operations in Afghanistan after the death of a US agent and 10 Afghan children in a battle he believes was fought by an illegal militia working for the US spy agency.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai suspended talks on a long-term security deal with the US and said he would not continue peace talks with the Taliban unless the US stepped out of the negotiations, amid a diplomatic row over how the Taliban peace process was announced.
President Hamid Karzai strongly condemned a Nato air strike in eastern Nangarhar province that he says killed five civilians, including three students.

Hamid Karzai rules out signing a security deal with the United States until disagreements over sovereignty are resolved, condemning Nato for a military occupation and casting doubt on whether the Bilateral Security Agreement would be renewed.

US Secretary of State John Kerry and Afghan President Hamid Karzai held talks in Kabul on a bilateral security agreement, resolving major issues but leaving the question of immunity for US troops to be decided by an assembly of elders and leaders.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai suggested that the bilateral security agreement with the US should only be signed after presidential elections next year, prompting a US warning that the deal must be signed before the end of this year.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai refused to sign the US-Afghan security pact despite the Loya Jirga's approval, saying he would continue talks with Washington and that the agreement should not be signed until after April presidential elections.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai outlined new conditions for signing the bilateral security agreement with the US and indicated he is not prepared to sign it promptly, after meeting with US national security adviser Susan Rice.
The Taliban urged Afghan President Hamid Karzai to reject the US security deal without conditions, after Karzai conditionally refused to sign the bilateral security agreement.
Hamid Karzai continues to refuse to sign a bilateral security agreement with the United States that would keep American troops in Afghanistan for the next 10 years.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai is reported to believe that many insurgent-style attacks in Afghanistan, including a recent suicide assault on a Kabul restaurant, were masterminded by the US, prompting a strong denial from the US envoy to Kabul.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai has reportedly been secretly directing peace negotiations with Taliban representatives for months, though no deal has been reached.
Afghanistan's upcoming presidential election is set to bring the country's first peaceful democratic transfer of power, as the constitution bars incumbent Hamid Karzai from standing again.
Hamid Karzai has reportedly been talking to the Taliban for several months in an attempt to broker a peace deal before his term expires, though the contacts have not yielded concrete results.
US director of national intelligence James Clapper says he does not believe Afghan president Hamid Karzai will sign the proposed bilateral security agreement for a long-term American troop presence.

Afghan president Hamid Karzai criticised a lack of US respect for Afghan sovereignty, saying the US should stop harassing Afghanistan's procedures and judicial authority and begin respecting Afghan sovereignty.
Hamid Karzai is due to step down after Afghanistan's presidential election, setting the stage for the country's first peaceful, democratic transfer of power.
Afghanistan held a presidential election to choose a successor to Hamid Karzai, who is barred by the constitution from seeking a third term.
Afghans voted in a presidential runoff election to choose a successor to President Hamid Karzai, marking the country's first democratic transfer of power.

Afghanistan faces a crisis over who will succeed Hamid Karzai as president, as preliminary election results give Ashraf Ghani a million-vote lead amid fraud accusations and warnings that no winner has yet been declared.
Afghanistan's president Hamid Karzai backs a UN plan to audit 3.5 million ballots for fraud in the disputed presidential poll, his spokesman says.
Outgoing Afghan President Hamid Karzai endorsed a UN proposal to audit 8,000 polling stations amid the standoff between presidential candidates Abdullah Abdullah and Ashraf Ghani.

Ashraf Ghani, Hamid Karzai's successor as president of Afghanistan, arrives in Islamabad for his first visit to Pakistan, which officials hope will mark a new chapter in Afghan-Pakistan relations after Karzai's difficult tenure.
Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai warned in a Guardian interview that Afghanistan is in danger of sliding "under the thumb" of Pakistan, criticizing successor Ashraf Ghani's overtures to Pakistan.

Former Afghan president Hamid Karzai is increasingly seen as a threat to Afghanistan's political stability, with a senior western diplomat saying he has been trying for months to undercut President Ashraf Ghani's government.
Hamid Karzai is described as a moderate Afghan political figure and former deputy foreign minister who is now attempting to hold together a fragile new coalition in Kabul.
US military intelligence reports allege that Pakistan's ISI plotted to assassinate Afghan President Hamid Karzai, though the predicted attack never took place.

A delegation of election experts found guarded optimism that Afghanistan's 2014 presidential election would be better run than the 2009 and 2010 polls, while noting concerns about fraud allegations, candidate exclusions, and the timeline for a likely runoff; Hamid Karzai's term was noted as ending in late May.
Hamid Karzai's adviser was assassinated.
